title: Integrate simulation into bead approval flow
description:
Wire the plan simulation into the bead approval flow in src/tools/approve.ts so simulation runs automatically before beads are presented for approval.

## Rationale
The best place to catch structural problems is right before beads are shown to the user for approval. If simulation finds issues, they should be displayed alongside the beads so the user (or LLM) can fix them before approving.

## Implementation

### Changes to src/tools/approve.ts:
1. Import simulateExecutionPaths and formatSimulationReport from plan-simulation.ts
2. After reading beads (readBeads call), construct SimulatedBead[] from the Bead[] using extractArtifacts
3. Get repo file list via a quick `find src -type f` or similar
4. Run simulateExecutionPaths and include the report in the approval output
5. If simulation finds issues, prepend a warning section to the approval message

### Changes to src/beads.ts:
1. Add a `simulationIssues` field to the validateBeads return type
2. Run simulation as part of validateBeads when called with beads that have file scope
3. Include simulation warnings alongside existing validation warnings

### Helper function:
- `beadsToSimulated(beads: Bead[])` — convert Bead[] to SimulatedBead[] using extractArtifacts for files and beadDeps for dependencies

### Files:
- src/tools/approve.ts
- src/beads.ts

### Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Simulation runs during bead approval flow
- [ ] Simulation results are included in the approval output message
- [ ] Issues are clearly formatted as warnings before the bead list
- [ ] A clean simulation shows a brief success confirmation
- [ ] beadsToSimulated correctly maps Bead fields to SimulatedBead fields
- [ ] npm run build passes
- [ ] Existing approve tests still pass

title: Extend verification evidence checks into a per-criterion proof matrix
description:
## Context
After pulling v1.3.4, this bead overlaps with existing closed work (`pi-r47`) in `src/bead-review.ts`: the code already parses verification commands and rejects generic evidence when a bead's `### Verification:` names exact commands. The remaining gap from the analyzed pi session is narrower: completion should produce a per-acceptance-criterion proof matrix, not only a command/evidence assessment.

## Why this bead still exists
The session failure mode was not just generic evidence; it was "implemented" work that did not satisfy every todo/bead Done When item. AgentFlywheel should explicitly map each acceptance criterion and verification check to evidence before allowing close/review pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Extend the existing verification evidence assessment instead of replacing it.
- [ ] Extract acceptance criteria from bead descriptions and produce a structured report with each criterion marked proven, unproven, blocked, or not applicable.
- [ ] Keep the existing exact-command evidence checks from `assessVerificationEvidence()` intact.
- [ ] Review output must distinguish command/check evidence from acceptance-criterion evidence.
- [ ] Generic "all tests passed" claims remain insufficient when exact commands or criteria are named.
- [ ] Add tests covering criterion-level proof, missing criterion evidence, exact command evidence, and manual fallback evidence.

### Verification:
- Commands/checks: run `npm run build` and `npm test -- src/bead-review.test.ts src/verification-contracts.integration.test.ts` or focused completion-checker tests.
- Success looks like: tests prove generic completion claims fail when exact commands/criteria are required, while explicit criterion-mapped evidence or documented fallback passes.
- Manual proof fallback: inspect the review output for a sample bead and verify every acceptance criterion is listed with a proof status.

### Files:
- src/bead-review.ts
- src/bead-review.test.ts
- src/tools/review.ts
- src/types.ts
notes: Extended verification evidence checks in src/bead-review.ts with acceptance-criterion proof tracking. Existing exact-command extraction and assessVerificationEvidence() behavior remain intact. Added extractAcceptanceCriteria(), assessAcceptanceCriteriaEvidence(), and formatAcceptanceCriteriaEvidenceMatrix() to produce per-criterion statuses: proven, unproven, blocked, or not_applicable. src/tools/review.ts now evaluates command/check evidence and acceptance-criterion evidence separately, returning distinct Command/check evidence and Acceptance-criterion evidence sections when a pass lacks proof. Generic completion claims remain insufficient when exact commands or criteria are named; documented manual fallback creates blocked criterion statuses rather than unproven failures. Added bead-review tests for criterion extraction, proven criteria, missing generic evidence, exact command evidence, and manual fallback evidence. Validation: npm test -- src/bead-review.test.ts src/verification-contracts.integration.test.ts passed (21 tests); npm run build passed; npm test passed (81 files, 1280 tests). Agent Mail still unreachable at localhost:8765.

title: Integrate simulation into approval and refinement
description:
Wire plan simulation into the bead approval flow (approve.ts) and add simulation-aware refinement prompts (prompts.ts).

## Rationale
The simulation module produces valuable pre-approval diagnostics. It should run automatically during bead approval and feed issues back into refinement prompts so the LLM can fix structural problems.

## Implementation

### Changes to src/tools/approve.ts:
1. Import simulateExecutionPaths, formatSimulationReport, beadsToSimulated from plan-simulation.ts
2. After reading beads via readBeads, build dep map via beadDeps calls, then call beadsToSimulated
3. Get repo file list via pi.exec('find', ['src', '-type', 'f']) (or similar lightweight scan)
4. Run simulateExecutionPaths and include formatSimulationReport output in the approval message
5. If simulation finds issues, prepend a warning section BEFORE the bead list
6. If simulation is clean, show a brief '✅ Simulation passed' line

### Changes to src/prompts.ts:
1. Add simulationRefinementPrompt(report: string, beadIds: string[]) — generates instructions referencing specific simulation failures with fix guidance per issue type:
   - File conflicts → split bead or add dependency edge
   - Missing files → update file paths or create the file
   - Execution order issues → adjust dependencies
2. Update freshContextRefinementPrompt to accept optional simulationReport parameter
3. When simulation issues exist, append them to refinement context

### Files:

- src/prompts.ts

- [ ] Simulation runs automatically during bead approval (orch_approve_beads flow)
- [ ] Simulation results appear in approval output before bead list

title: Cover fresh-eyes review workflow with docs and tests
description:
## Goal
Document and test the fresh-eyes reviewer workflow so future agents understand when the reviewer runs, how Agent Mail coordination works, how findings get appended back onto the current bead, and how to troubleshoot degraded review runs.

## Rationale
A background reviewer that wakes up every 7 minutes, waits for 5 new commits, launches through Agent Mail, and appends findings onto the active bead spans orchestration, prompts, bead updates, and failure handling. Without explicit docs and regression tests, the feature will drift or become undiscoverable for later operators.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add or update tests proving the 7-minute / 5-commit launch policy, current-bead append behavior, non-actionable no-op behavior, and graceful handling of Agent Mail/subagent failures.
- [ ] Update user- or agent-facing documentation/help text so it explicitly states that fresh-eyes review runs during implementation, uses Agent Mail coordination, performs a full review, and appends findings onto the current bead. README.md currently only name-drops "fresh eyes" in the feature list and architecture diagram; this bead must add a dedicated subsection that names the 7-minute cadence, 5-commit threshold, Agent Mail thread usage, current-bead append behavior, and how the feature degrades.
- [ ] Include at least one concrete example of a finding that should be appended to the bead and one comment that should be ignored or summarized instead.
- [ ] Add troubleshooting guidance for cases where the reviewer never launches, returns no findings, or cannot update the bead.
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass after implementation.

### Verification:
- Commands/checks: run `npm test` and `npm run build`; if documentation assertions or snapshot-style tests exist for prompts/help text, run those too.
- Success looks like: automated coverage includes launch cadence, append behavior, and degraded failures; docs/help text matches the implemented thresholds and Agent Mail flow; and the standard build/test commands pass cleanly.
- Manual proof fallback: if automation cannot cover the full live subagent loop, compare the updated docs/examples against the launch and append code paths to confirm they describe the same 7-minute cadence, 5-commit threshold, full-review scope, thread usage, and failure handling.

### Files:
- README.md — primary user-facing docs target. Today it only mentions "fresh eyes" in the feature/diagram lists; add a dedicated subsection covering cadence, threshold, Agent Mail thread usage, current-bead append behavior, and troubleshooting.
- AGENTS.md — extend the Agent Mail / workflow guidance only if operator-facing thread, callsign, or coordination conventions change specifically for fresh-eyes runs.
- src/fresh-eyes-review.test.ts — canonical test home. Strengthen coverage for the 7-min / 5-commit launch policy, current-bead append (including duplicate-suppression and non-actionable no-op), and Agent Mail / subagent failure degradation.
- src/fresh-eyes-review.ts — source of truth for any docs examples (`FRESH_EYES_REVIEW_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, `FRESH_EYES_REVIEW_LAUNCH_AFTER_COMMITS`, `FRESH_EYES_REVIEW_HEADING`). Keep docs in lockstep with these constants so the cadence/threshold/heading never drift.
- src/prompts.ts — touch only if the operator-facing reviewer prompt/help text moves here or is referenced from external surfaces.

title: Build Flywheel swarm forecast input adapter
description:

Why this bead exists:
- The pure forecast engine intentionally consumes saved JSON only; Flywheel still needs a thin adapter that translates current beads, dependencies, files, validation lanes, known agents, and reservations into that saved input.
- Keeping this adapter separate preserves the safety boundary between live collection and pure forecasting.

Scope:
- Add a helper that accepts current Bead[] plus optional Agent Mail reservation/agent/activity data and returns a SwarmForecastInput object.
- Extract touched files from bead descriptions using existing artifact helpers rather than re-parsing unrelated syntax.
- Infer validation lanes from verification contracts and common command strings such as npm test, vitest, npm run build, tsc, pytest, br/bv checks, and package scripts used in this repo.
- Populate conservative build-lane defaults for this TypeScript project: npm/vitest/typecheck/build and generic CLI validation lanes.
- Treat Agent Mail data as optional/fail-open; unavailable sources should become source warnings, not thrown errors.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Adapter produces valid saved input from realistic Bead objects without calling the forecast engine.
- [ ] Dependencies, statuses, priorities, labels, files, and validation lanes are mapped deterministically.
- [ ] Agent Mail reservations/agents/activity are optional and sanitized before entering forecast input.
- [ ] Missing Agent Mail or bv/br metadata does not throw; the saved input records source uncertainty if needed.
- [ ] Unit tests cover ready/open/in_progress/closed beads, dependencies, file extraction, validation-lane inference, stale reservations, and unavailable optional sources.
- [ ] Adapter does not mutate bead status, reservations, Git, or files except when explicitly asked by a caller to write the saved input artifact.

### Verification:

- Success looks like: adapter tests pass with mocked bead/reservation inputs, TypeScript compiles, and the adapter can produce saved input without requiring live Agent Mail or br commands.

title: Add template hygiene checks to bead validation and approval
description:
Protect the new bead-template workflow from degrading final bead quality by extending automated bead validation checks to flag unresolved template artifacts. Once templates are introduced, the validateBeads() function should reject beads that still contain raw template markers, unresolved placeholders, or other shorthand that a fresh implementing agent cannot act on directly.

### Why this bead is needed
Prompt guidance alone is helpful but insufficient. The approval pipeline already runs bead validation via validateBeads(); this feature should teach that function about template-specific failure modes so bad beads are caught before implementation starts.

### Failure modes to detect
Add new validation rules to catch bead descriptions that contain any of the following:
- Raw template markers such as '[Use template:' or 'Use template:' at the start of lines
- 'see template' / 'use the template' shorthand with no expanded implementation details
- Unresolved placeholder syntax: {{placeholderName}}, <placeholder>, or similar TODO-style substitution markers
- Template-generated sections with no concrete file scope or acceptance criteria after expansion (detected via missing Files: section or empty acceptance criteria when template markers are also present)

### Implementation scope
- Extend validateBeads() in src/beads.ts with template-hygiene validation rules that run alongside existing validation checks
- Add a new validation category (e.g., "template_hygiene") to the validation result structure
- Each validation failure should include the bead ID, the specific issue found, and the line/excerpt where the problem appears
- Keep the checks specific enough to catch obvious template leakage without over-flagging legitimate prose that mentions templates in documentation context
- The checks should only fire on beads with status="open" since closed/wip beads may legitimately have drafty content

### Detection patterns (implementation guidance)
- For raw template markers: Check for lines matching /^\s*\[?Use template:/i or /^\s*see template/i at the start of description paragraphs
- For unresolved placeholders: Check for {{\w+}} patterns or <\w+> patterns that look like unfilled template variables (not HTML tags or comparison operators)
- For template-without-expansion: If any template markers found, also check that the bead has a non-empty Files: section and at least 2 acceptance criteria items

### Integration with existing validation
- validateBeads() already returns an array of validation issues
- Add template hygiene issues to that same array with clear error messages
- Existing approval/review flows that consume validateBeads() output will automatically surface these failures
- No changes needed to src/tools/approve.ts or src/tools/review.ts unless the validation message format changes

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Add template hygiene validation logic to validateBeads() in src/beads.ts
- [ ] Validation catches raw '[Use template: ...]' or 'Use template:' markers at the start of description lines
- [ ] Validation catches 'see template' / 'use the template' shorthand references
- [ ] Validation catches unresolved {{placeholder}} syntax in bead descriptions
- [ ] Validation catches <placeholder> syntax that looks like unfilled template variables (not HTML/operators)
- [ ] Validation only checks beads with status="open" (ignores closed/wip beads)
- [ ] Each validation failure includes: bead ID, issue type, and excerpt/line showing the problem
- [ ] Add tests in src/beads.test.ts covering both pass and fail cases for template hygiene
- [ ] Tests verify that beads with '[Use template: add-api-endpoint]' are flagged
- [ ] Tests verify that beads with 'see template' shorthand are flagged
- [ ] Tests verify that beads with unresolved {{endpointPath}} markers are flagged
- [ ] Tests verify that beads mentioning 'template' in legitimate documentation context (e.g., "this follows the singleton template pattern") are NOT flagged
- [ ] Tests verify that closed beads with template markers are NOT flagged
- [ ] npm test passes after the new validation logic is added
- [ ] Existing approval/review flows surface template hygiene failures without additional code changes

### Files:

- src/beads.test.ts
- src/types.ts (if validation result structure needs adjustment)
- src/tools/approve.ts (reference only - no changes expected unless message formatting needs work)

title: Migrate remaining profile/dashboard br recovery call sites
description:
Migrate the remaining `br` call sites in `src/tools/profile.ts` and `src/index.ts` so discovery and dashboard flows degrade cleanly when `br` is flaky or unavailable mid-session.

## What to implement

### `src/tools/profile.ts`
- Deep-discovery bead-title preload: `br list --json` → `brExecJson`
- Deferred-bead reactivation loop: `br update <id> --status open` → `brExec`
- Clear-beads flow: `br delete ... --force --hard` and fallback `--force` → `brExec`

### `src/index.ts`
- Dashboard unblocked-bead lookup: `br ready --json` → `brExecJson`

## Migration rules
1. Preserve today’s fallbacks exactly:
   - deep discovery still falls back to `readBeads()` and then to an empty title list
   - reactivation loop remains best-effort and continues past individual failures
   - clear-beads flow still tries `--force --hard` first, then `--force`, then shows the existing warning
   - dashboard widget still returns `[]` when unblocked-bead lookup fails
2. The new wrapper results must carry structured error detail even when the public return value degrades to `[]` / empty state
3. Do not broaden scope into unrelated `pi.exec` sites that are not part of `br`-driven recovery in these files

## Why this matters
These call sites are user-visible. If `br` is unavailable mid-session, discovery should still continue, the dashboard should keep rendering, and clear/reactivate flows should fail gracefully instead of disappearing into raw catch blocks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All direct `br` execs in `src/tools/profile.ts` and `src/index.ts` are migrated to `brExec` / `brExecJson`
- [ ] Existing fallback behavior is preserved for deep discovery, reactivation, clear-beads, and dashboard unblocked-bead lookup
- [ ] `src/tools/profile.ts` no longer contains silent `br` best-effort catches
- [ ] Relevant tests (`src/commands.test.ts`, `src/coordination.test.ts`, or a new focused test file) cover at least: dashboard returns `[]` on failed `br ready --json`, discovery falls back past failed `br list --json`, and clear-beads still shows the existing manual-warning path after both delete attempts fail
- [ ] `npm run build` passes

title: fresh-eyes-current-bead-append
description:
Append fresh-eyes review output to the current bead in a bounded, idempotent section.

High-level design context:
- The review subagent reports through Agent Mail. Those findings need to become visible to implementation agents in the bead they are already executing.
- This bead owns the transformation from reviewer output/launch metadata into a safe current-bead description/comment update.
- It depends on `fresh-eyes-agent-mail-launch` because it should use the launch/thread/reviewer metadata produced there.

Data model / types context:
- Consume the existing fresh-eyes state fields: `threadId`, `reviewerAgentName`, `launchedForHead`, and `currentBeadId`.
- Add a small append input/result type only if needed, with fields for timestamp, reviewer, thread ID, head ref, findings, suggested actions, clean-pass status, and a stable idempotency key.
- Keep the data shape serializable and testable so later implementation-loop integration can call it without depending on UI objects.
- If an idempotency marker is stored in the bead body, use a deterministic marker such as an HTML comment keyed by thread/reviewer/head instead of hidden global state.

New internal functions / boundaries to make explicit:
- `buildFreshEyesAppendKey(...)` creates the stable duplicate-suppression key from thread/head/reviewer inputs.
- `renderFreshEyesReviewBlock(...)` formats the bounded markdown section, including clean-pass output.
- `appendFreshEyesReviewToBead(...)` owns the read/modify/write flow through existing bead helpers.
- `findExistingFreshEyesEntry(...)` or equivalent checks the current bead body for the same idempotency marker before mutating anything.

Mocking strategy:
- Test rendering/idempotency logic with in-memory bead description strings or existing bead helper seams, not shelling out to real `br` commands.
- Mock only the bead read/update boundary needed for append behavior; keep markdown rendering and duplicate detection pure.
- Cover duplicate suppression, clean-pass rendering, missing-current-bead warnings, and multi-entry behavior (same heading, different triggering head).

Edge cases & failure modes:
- Missing current bead ID must return a clear warning/result and must not mutate an arbitrary bead.
- Existing bead descriptions without a trailing newline, with prior fresh-eyes sections, or with malformed markers must still produce readable output without corrupting the bead.
- Empty findings should produce a short clean-pass note, not a noisy placeholder wall of text.
- Different triggering heads or different reviewer/thread pairs must append a new entry instead of collapsing distinct reviews together.
- Unexpected bead update/read failures must surface a clear non-fatal result so the implementation loop can continue.

What to implement:
- Add a safe helper that appends fresh-eyes review findings or clean-pass notes to the current bead.
- The appended section must be self-contained and bounded, for example `## Fresh-Eyes Review Findings`, with timestamp, reviewer, Agent Mail thread, triggering head, findings, and suggested actions.
- Avoid duplicate append blocks for the same reviewer/thread/head combination when the poller or parent process retries.
- If no current bead can be determined, return a clear warning and do not crash or mutate an arbitrary bead.
- Use existing bead/CLI helpers rather than ad-hoc text manipulation from shell commands.

Key decisions and trade-offs:
- Append to the current bead rather than creating a detached follow-up task by default, because active implementers need feedback in their immediate work context.
- Use a bounded section and idempotency key so retries and polling do not spam bead descriptions.
- Do not launch reviewers here; this bead should be a pure-ish append/update boundary.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Review findings append to the known current bead with a clear `Fresh-Eyes Review Findings` heading.
- [ ] The append content includes reviewer, Agent Mail thread, triggering head, timestamp, concise actionable bullets, and a stable idempotency key/marker.
- [ ] Re-running the append path for the same review does not duplicate the same block.
- [ ] Different triggering heads or different reviewer/thread pairs create distinct entries instead of overwriting each other.
- [ ] Missing current bead is handled with a warning/result and no crash.
- [ ] Clean-pass/no-finding notes are short and do not create noisy placeholder tasks.
- [ ] Tests cover append, duplicate suppression, clean-pass/no-finding note, malformed-existing-section handling, and missing-current-bead cases.

title: Add built-in bead template library primitives
description:
Build the reusable bead-template foundation that planning flows can reference instead of inventing every bead shape from scratch. Create a typed template system that exposes a small built-in catalog of common planning patterns (add-api-endpoint, refactor-module, add-tests) with concrete examples and clear extension points. The output should be deterministic, dependency-free, and easy for prompt builders, approval flows, and future TUI surfaces to render, inspect, and instantiate.

### Why this bead exists
This is the architectural base for the entire feature. Downstream prompt, validation, documentation, and integration-test work should consume this shared catalog instead of duplicating template definitions or hard-coded strings.

### Template model requirements
Add a BeadTemplate type that is specific enough for both prompt generation and future UI rendering. Each template must include:
- Stable template ID (e.g. add-api-endpoint)
- Human-readable label
- One-line summary for prompt listings
- Description template text with explicit placeholder markers (using {{placeholderName}} syntax)
- Placeholder metadata describing each placeholder (name, description, example value, whether required)
- Default acceptance-criteria checklist entries (can include placeholders)
- Typical file patterns as an array of glob strings (for example: ["src/api/*.ts", "tests/**/*.test.ts"])
- Optional dependency hints as free-form text guidance (for example: "add-tests usually depends on an implementation bead")
- At least one fully expanded example showing what a finished instantiated bead description looks like

### Placeholder format specification
The expandTemplate() function should accept placeholders as Record<string, string> where keys match placeholder names in the template (without the {{}} markers). For example: { endpoint: "/users", module: "user-auth" }

### Error handling specification
- expandTemplate() should return a Result type (success | error) or throw a descriptive error when:
  - The requested template ID does not exist
  - Required placeholders are missing from the provided substitution map
  - Placeholder values contain invalid characters that would break bead descriptions
- Do not silently generate misleading descriptions or leave unresolved {{markers}} in output
- Error messages should clearly identify which placeholder is missing or invalid

### Initial built-in catalog
Ship these three templates in the first version:
1. add-api-endpoint — REST/GraphQL endpoint with validation, error handling, and tests
2. refactor-module — extract/reorganize code while preserving behavior
3. add-tests — add unit/integration coverage for existing functionality

### Required helper APIs
Export helpers from src/bead-templates.ts that are usable by prompt code and tests:
- listBeadTemplates(): BeadTemplate[] — return the full built-in catalog in deterministic order
- formatTemplatesForPrompt(): string — return a compact prompt-safe listing (id + one-line summary + placeholder names)
- getTemplateById(templateId: string): BeadTemplate | undefined — return the template definition or undefined
- expandTemplate(templateId: string, placeholders: Record<string, string>): { success: true; description: string } | { success: false; error: string } — return a ready-to-paste self-contained bead description with placeholders substituted, or an error

### Behavioral expectations
- Deterministic output: repeated calls return stable ordering and formatting
- No new runtime dependencies beyond existing project dependencies (TypeScript, testing libs already in package.json are OK)
- Expansion should fail clearly with descriptive errors when template ID is invalid or required placeholders are missing
- Expanded output must be suitable for passing directly to br create --description after caller customization
- Examples and placeholder names should push agents toward concrete, self-contained bead descriptions rather than vague shorthand
- Template descriptions should use {{placeholderName}} syntax consistently (e.g., {{endpointPath}}, {{moduleName}}, {{testFiles}})

- [ ] Each template includes at least one fully expanded example

title: Core episodic memory module (src/episodic-memory.ts)
description:
Create src/episodic-memory.ts — the foundational module that wraps the python -m mempalace CLI, mirroring the pattern of src/memory.ts which wraps the cm CASS CLI.

## Background

pi-orchestrator uses CASS (cm CLI) for procedural memory — rules and bullets distilled from past sessions. MemPalace is a complementary episodic memory store (ChromaDB + all-MiniLM-L6-v2) that stores verbatim session text and retrieves it via semantic search at 96.6% LongMemEval R@5.

The integration is optional and gracefully degrading: if mempalace is not installed, all functions return empty/false and orchestration is unaffected.

## What to implement

Create src/episodic-memory.ts with these 5 exported functions:

### detectMempalace(): boolean
- Run python3 -m mempalace --version with 3s timeout
- Cache true permanently (process lifetime), cache false for 5s (same pattern as detectCass() in memory.ts)
- Return false on any error (ENOENT, timeout, non-zero exit, crash)
- Module-level: _mempalaceAvailable: boolean | null = null, _mempalaceCheckedAt = 0, MEMPALACE_FALSE_CACHE_MS = 5_000

### mineSession(transcriptPath: string, projectSlug: string): boolean
- Shells out: python3 -m mempalace mine <transcriptPath> --mode convos --wing <projectSlug> --extract general
- Timeout: 10s
- Returns true on exit 0, false otherwise. Never throws.

### searchEpisodic(query: string, options?: { wing?: string; nResults?: number }): string
- Shells out: python3 -m mempalace search <query> --json --n <nResults> (default nResults=5)
- Add --wing <wing> if options.wing provided
- Timeout: 10s
- Parses JSON output (array of: { text, similarity, wing, room, metadata })
- Formats results as: [pi-orchestrator / decisions] (sim=0.91)\n  <text excerpt>
- Returns empty string if detectMempalace() false, CLI errors, or no results

### getEpisodicContext(task: string, projectSlug: string): string
- Calls searchEpisodic(task, { wing: projectSlug, nResults: 5 })
- If non-empty, wraps in: ## Past Session Examples header
- Returns empty string if not available or no results

### getEpisodicStats(): EpisodicStats
- Shells out: python3 -m mempalace status --json
- Parses for path and drawer count
- Returns { available: false, palacePath: null, drawerCount: 0 } on any error

## Types to define
export interface EpisodicResult {
  text: string;
  similarity: number;
  wing: string;
  room: string;
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export interface EpisodicStats {
  available: boolean;
  palacePath: string | null;
  drawerCount: number;
}

## Key implementation notes
- Import execFileSync from child_process (same as memory.ts)
- Use python3 (not python) for macOS compatibility
- All functions wrapped in try/catch returning empty/false on any error
- JSON parsing: JSON.parse(output.toString().trim()) with fallback

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] detectMempalace() returns boolean, caches true permanently / false for 5s
- [ ] mineSession() constructs correct CLI args: mine, path, --mode convos, --wing slug, --extract general
- [ ] searchEpisodic() returns formatted string with sim scores and wing/room labels
- [ ] searchEpisodic() returns empty string when mempalace not available
- [ ] getEpisodicContext() wraps results in ## Past Session Examples header
- [ ] getEpisodicStats() returns typed struct, never throws
- [ ] All functions return empty/false on any error (no throws bubble up)
- [ ] npm run build passes with zero type errors

title: Turn fresh-eyes review findings into beads
description:
## Goal
When the fresh-eyes reviewer finds actionable problems, append those findings back onto the bead currently being implemented so review debt stays attached to the live work item instead of disappearing into transient logs. The default behavior should be to enrich the current bead with structured findings, not to spray disconnected notes across the workflow.

## Rationale
The requested workflow says the fresh-eyes reviewer should "add to the beads," and the implementation notes further narrow that to appending onto the current bead. That means this bead owns the finding-to-bead update path: parse review output, keep only actionable findings, dedupe reruns, and write back a stable, readable section that later implementers and reviewers can trust.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Parse full fresh-eyes review output into structured candidate findings that preserve severity, rationale/evidence, affected files or surfaces, and the concrete implementation/acceptance delta being called out.
- [ ] Append validated actionable findings to the current bead description under a predictable fresh-eyes findings section, and make reruns idempotent so the same finding is not appended repeatedly. The established convention is a single `## Fresh-Eyes Review Findings` heading (`FRESH_EYES_REVIEW_HEADING` in src/fresh-eyes-review.ts) plus a per-entry HTML-comment marker of the shape `<!-- fresh-eyes-review:<key> -->`; preserve both when extending the dedupe key or the rendered shape.
- [ ] Keep appended text self-contained enough that a fresh implementer or reviewer can act on it without reopening subagent logs: include why it matters, what needs to change, and where to look.
- [ ] Non-actionable comments, compliments, or low-signal chatter are either omitted or collapsed into a short summary so bead descriptions stay readable.
- [ ] If bead lookup or append/update fails, surface a clear warning/result and keep the main implementation workflow alive.

### Verification:
- Commands/checks: run `npm test` and `npm run build`; if there are targeted tests for review parsing or bead updates, run those suites against duplicate, actionable, and non-actionable finding fixtures.
- Success looks like: actionable findings are appended onto the active bead in a stable section, repeated identical findings do not duplicate entries, non-actionable comments do not create noisy bead churn, and append failures return/report a degraded result instead of crashing.
- Manual proof fallback: if automation cannot exercise live `br` updates end-to-end, inspect the parsing helper, append formatter, and bead-update boundary with representative fixtures to confirm severity/evidence/file hints are preserved and duplicate findings collapse correctly.

### Files:
- src/fresh-eyes-review.ts — canonical home for parsing, formatting, and idempotent append (`appendFreshEyesReviewToBead`, `FreshEyesAppendInput`, `FreshEyesBeadAppendBoundary`, finding-block builder, `FRESH_EYES_REVIEW_HEADING`, idempotency-marker helper). Extend severity-rubric parsing, non-actionable filtering, and dedupe-key derivation here.
- src/tools/review.ts — invokes `appendFreshEyesReviewToBead` after the fresh-eyes monitor returns findings (around the post-accept tick). Widen the call site here to thread severity-tagged output and to bubble degraded append results.
- src/beads.ts — touch only if a new bead-update primitive is required beyond what the append boundary already wraps (e.g., a richer description-patch helper). Prefer keeping bead I/O in the existing boundary abstraction.
- src/prompts.ts — touch only if the reviewer's output contract changes (e.g., a new severity rubric) and downstream parsers need to align.
- src/fresh-eyes-review.test.ts — add fixtures for duplicate, actionable, and non-actionable findings; cover preserved heading/marker behavior across reruns, severity/evidence/file-hint preservation, and graceful surfacing when the bead-update boundary fails.

title: Add beads-workflow Quality Checklist as a pre-implementation validation gate
description:
## Context
The `/beads-workflow` skill defines an 8-item Quality Checklist that must pass before implementation begins: self-contained, clear scope, explicit dependencies, testable, includes tests, preserves features, not oversimplified, no cycles. The flywheel's current quality gate (`qualityCheckBeads()` in approve.ts) runs structural checks (verification contract, files section) but does not systematically verify the 'includes tests', 'not oversimplified', and 'clear scope' dimensions from the beads-workflow checklist.

## Rationale
Agents frequently produce beads that pass structural checks (has a Verification section, has a Files section) but still fail the softer quality dimensions: no companion test beads, scope that spans 5+ files with no subtask breakdown, or descriptions so terse they require reading the original plan. The beads-workflow Quality Checklist is the industry-tested remedy, applied across 100+ sessions.

- [ ] The checklist items use the exact beads-workflow language: Self-contained, Clear scope, Dependencies explicit, Testable, Includes tests, Preserves features, Not oversimplified, No cycles
- [ ] The 'No cycles' item is linked to the live `br dep cycles` result already computed by the approval flow (show ✅ or ⚠️ inline)
- [ ] The checklist is shown as a reference/reminder, NOT as a blocking gate that prevents proceeding — the user can still start implementing if they acknowledge it

title: Document MemPalace setup in AGENTS.md
description:
Update AGENTS.md to document the optional MemPalace episodic memory integration — installation steps, the wing convention, and what happens when it is not installed.

## Background

pi-orchestrator now has two complementary memory systems:
1. CASS (cm CLI): procedural memory — rules distilled from past sessions
2. MemPalace (python -m mempalace): episodic memory — verbatim session text, retrieved by semantic search

MemPalace is entirely optional. If not installed, pi-orchestrator works exactly as before. AGENTS.md should document this for contributors and users who want richer context.

## What to add to AGENTS.md

Add a new section after the existing memory/CASS documentation. Something like:

### Episodic Memory (MemPalace) — Optional

pi-orchestrator supports optional episodic memory via MemPalace. While CASS stores extracted rules, MemPalace stores verbatim session text and retrieves it via semantic search (96.6% LongMemEval R@5).

**Setup (one-time):**
  pip install mempalace
  python3 -m mempalace init

**What it does:**
- When an orchestration reaches two clean review rounds, the session transcript is mined into MemPalace
- During bead planning, relevant past sessions are retrieved and injected into the planning prompt
- Wing name: the project directory basename (e.g. pi-orchestrator), so sessions are grouped per project

**Graceful degradation:**
- If mempalace is not installed, orchestration runs normally with no changes
- No errors, no warnings — detection is silent

**Detection:** pi-orchestrator runs python3 -m mempalace --version at startup (3s timeout). If it succeeds, episodic memory is enabled for that process.

**Wing convention:** All sessions for a project share one MemPalace wing named after path.basename(cwd) with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by hyphens. E.g. /Volumes/1tb/Projects/pi-orchestrator uses wing pi-orchestrator.

**Room assignment:** MemPalace's built-in general extractor classifies chunks into: decisions, preferences, milestones, problems, emotional. This happens automatically during mining (--extract general flag).

**Why not use AAAK compression?**
Benchmarks show AAAK compresses to 84.2% vs raw 96.6% on LongMemEval. Compression discards semantic content. pi-orchestrator always uses L3 direct semantic search (mempalace search) for highest accuracy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AGENTS.md has a new MemPalace section with installation steps (pip install mempalace, python3 -m mempalace init)
- [ ] Section documents graceful degradation (works fine without mempalace)
- [ ] Wing naming convention documented (basename + hyphen sanitisation)
- [ ] Room assignment and --extract general documented
- [ ] Explains CASS vs MemPalace distinction (rules vs verbatim episodes)
- [ ] Section is concise — no more than ~30 lines

title: Core checkpoint module
description:
Create src/checkpoint.ts with atomic write-rename checkpoint persistence.

## What to build
A new module src/checkpoint.ts that handles all disk I/O for orchestration checkpoints. The checkpoint file lives at <cwd>/.pi-orchestrator/checkpoint.json.

## Checkpoint Envelope
Add CheckpointEnvelope interface to src/types.ts:
- schemaVersion: 1
- writtenAt: string (ISO timestamp)
- orchestratorVersion: string
- gitHead?: string (current git HEAD for branch-change detection)
- state: OrchestratorState
- stateHash: string (SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(state))

## Functions to implement in src/checkpoint.ts
- CHECKPOINT_DIR = '.pi-orchestrator', CHECKPOINT_FILE = 'checkpoint.json'
- writeCheckpoint(cwd, state, orchestratorVersion): boolean — atomic write via tmp+rename, never throws
- readCheckpoint(cwd): { envelope: CheckpointEnvelope, warnings: string[] } | null — validates JSON, schema version, hash; moves corrupt files to .corrupt; warns if >24h stale
- clearCheckpoint(cwd): void — idempotent delete
- validateCheckpoint(envelope: unknown): { valid: true } | { valid: false, reason: string }

## Key requirements
- All I/O is non-throwing — errors caught and logged, return false/null
- Atomic write: writeFileSync to checkpoint.json.tmp, then renameSync to checkpoint.json
- Hash: crypto.createHash('sha256') of JSON.stringify(state)
- Corrupt files: rename to checkpoint.json.corrupt for inspection
- Staleness: if writtenAt is >24h old, add warning string to warnings array
- Git HEAD: try execSync('git rev-parse HEAD') silently, store if available

title: fresh-eyes-implementation-loop-integration
description:
Integrate the fresh-eyes monitor into the active implementation loop so it checks every 7 minutes and launches once after 5 commits.

High-level design context:
- Implementation proceeds through the existing flywheel bead workflow.
- A monitor records a baseline at implementation start, checks progress on a 7-minute cadence, and asks the launch boundary to start one full fresh-eyes review after 5 new commits.
- Agent Mail is used for reviewer coordination, and review findings are appended to the current bead by the append helper.
- Existing final review gates remain authoritative; this is an earlier risk-reduction pass.

Component relationships:
- Use the pure threshold/state helpers from `src/fresh-eyes-review.ts`.
- Use the Agent Mail launch boundary from `fresh-eyes-agent-mail-launch`.
- Use the current-bead append boundary from `fresh-eyes-current-bead-append`.
- Persist monitor state in the existing checkpoint/session state path if compatible; avoid inventing a parallel persistence system.
- Integrate in the narrowest existing implementation-wave/tender loop that is active while agents are implementing.

Data model / types context:
- Extend the existing checkpoint/session/orchestrator state with a serializable fresh-eyes monitor block that stores: enabled flag, baseline head/ref, baseline commit count, last checked timestamp, launched flag, launched timestamp, launched head, thread ID, reviewer agent name, and current bead ID snapshot.
- Treat missing legacy state as "not initialized yet" rather than a hard migration failure.
- Keep config defaults at 5 commits and 420000ms; integration should not hard-code different values.
- Persist state transitions in a way that preserves at-most-once semantics across retries/resumes: baseline write before polling, launched metadata write only after a real launch, and clear last-known status text for observability.

New internal functions / boundaries to make explicit:
- `initializeFreshEyesMonitorState(...)` captures the baseline when implementation begins.
- `shouldPollFreshEyesReview(...)` or equivalent enforces the 7-minute cadence from explicit timestamps, not sleeping loops inside tests.
- `runFreshEyesMonitorTick(...)` gathers current git/bead context, asks the pure core whether to launch, and delegates side effects to the launch boundary.
- `persistFreshEyesMonitorOutcome(...)` merges waiting/launched/skipped/degraded results back into checkpoint/session state.

Mocking strategy:
- Inject fakes for git/head lookup, commit-count calculation, clock/now timestamps, checkpoint persistence, and the launch boundary.
- Use explicit timestamps in tests to simulate the 7-minute cadence; do not use real timers or real sleeps.
- Cover baseline setup, below-threshold polling, threshold reached, duplicate polling after launch, degraded launch boundary response, disabled config, and resume-from-existing-state behavior.

Edge cases & failure modes:
- Resume/retry after a previous successful launch must not launch again for the same head.
- Git/commit-count lookup failure, detached-head-like states, or missing current bead context must degrade with clear status text instead of crashing.
- If implementation ends before threshold, the monitor should stop quietly without inventing extra work.
- If more than 5 commits accumulate between polls, the first eligible poll should still launch exactly once.
- Disabled config or unavailable Agent Mail must preserve the pre-existing implementation/review workflow with no behavior regressions.
- If the append boundary later fails, the monitor must still record whether launch occurred and expose the degraded append status separately rather than losing launch history.

What to implement:
- Locate the existing implementation-wave/tender loop that runs while agents are actively implementing approved beads.
- Record the fresh-eyes baseline at implementation start using the current HEAD or equivalent commit count.
- Add a poll/tick integration with a 7-minute cadence that calls the fresh-eyes launch helper while implementation is active.
- Persist enough state to avoid duplicate launches across retries/resumes.
- Ensure the existing plan/approve/implement/review workflow remains unchanged when the feature is disabled, when Agent Mail is unavailable, or when there are fewer than 5 commits.
- Surface clear status text for launched, waiting, skipped, and degraded states.

Key decisions and trade-offs:
- Polling avoids mutating user git hooks and works across parallel agents, at the cost of not launching instantly at the fifth commit.
- Commit threshold prevents launching too early in slow or idle sessions.
- Fail-open behavior keeps implementation moving even when git/Agent Mail/reviewer launch is unavailable.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Implementation start records a baseline ref/count for the fresh-eyes monitor.
- [ ] The active implementation loop checks on a 7-minute cadence while work is in progress.
- [ ] The checkpoint/session state stores baseline, last-check, launched, thread, reviewer, and current-bead snapshot fields in a serializable shape that survives resume.
- [ ] The fresh-eyes review launches exactly once after at least 5 new commits since baseline, including when the first eligible poll observes more than 5 commits.
- [ ] The current bead ID, if known, flows into Agent Mail instructions and bead append behavior.
- [ ] Existing implementation/review flows still work with the feature disabled, with missing legacy state, or when launch dependencies degrade.
- [ ] Tests cover baseline setup, below-threshold polling, launch at threshold, launch after skipped polls, duplicate polling after launch, degraded git/Agent Mail paths, and resume behavior.
- [ ] `npm run build` and full `npm test` pass.

### Verification:
- Commands/checks:
  - `npm test -- src/swarm.test.ts src/checkpoint.test.ts src/fresh-eyes-review.test.ts`
  - `npm run build`
  - `npm test`
- Success looks like: focused tests prove baseline persistence, explicit 7-minute cadence gating, threshold launch, resume/idempotency, and degraded-path handling; then the full TypeScript build and full Vitest suite finish without failures.
- Manual proof fallback: if commands cannot run, capture the exact blocker and inspect the integration call site, persisted state updates, and tests to confirm baseline setup, cadence enforcement, at-most-once launch, resume-safe serialization, and non-fatal degradation behavior.

title: fresh-eyes-agent-mail-launch
description:
Wire the fresh-eyes review launch boundary to Agent Mail and subagent instructions without making implementation fragile when coordination is unavailable.

High-level design context:
- The fresh-eyes review monitor has a pure core that decides when a full review should launch after 5 commits.
- This bead owns the side-effect boundary that turns a launch decision into an Agent Mail-coordinated reviewer request.
- It must not decide commit thresholds itself; consume the core config/state/result types and keep launch side effects isolated.

Component relationships:
- Consume `FreshEyesReviewConfig`, `FreshEyesReviewState`, and `FreshEyesReviewLaunchResult` from the core helper/types.
- Reuse existing Agent Mail helper patterns in `src/agent-mail.ts` for project identity, thread selection, and message sending.
- Keep `src/fresh-eyes-review.ts` as the single public surface for review-launch orchestration so later implementation-loop integration has one function to call.
- Do not append bead findings in this bead; that is owned by `fresh-eyes-current-bead-append` and depends on this launch metadata.

Data model / types context:
- Add or extend a narrow launch-context/input type that carries: current bead ID (optional), existing thread ID (optional), launched-for head, baseline head, commit delta, run/session identifier, and the full prompt text produced by the pure core.
- Return a structured launch outcome type or discriminated union with `status: 'launched' | 'skipped' | 'degraded'`, plus explicit `reasonCode`, human-readable `reason`, and launch metadata fields (`threadId`, `reviewerAgentName`, `launchedAt`, `launchedForHead`) only when valid.
- Keep the Agent Mail boundary injected behind a minimal interface so tests can fake thread resolution, message send, and optional reviewer/subagent launch without importing real MCP clients.

New internal functions / boundaries to make explicit:
- `resolveFreshEyesThread(...)` chooses current-bead thread first, then falls back to a run-level thread with an explicit reason.
- `buildFreshEyesLaunchEnvelope(...)` converts the pure-core prompt plus launch metadata into the exact Agent Mail/subagent request payload.
- `launchFreshEyesViaAgentMail(...)` performs the side effects and maps raw failures into the structured launch outcome.
- `mergeLaunchSuccessIntoState(...)` records thread/reviewer/head metadata only after a real launch success.

Mocking strategy:
- Mock the Agent Mail boundary at the module edge instead of mocking the pure launch-decision helper.
- Use table-driven tests for: existing current-bead thread, run-level fallback thread, send failure, Agent Mail unavailable, malformed current bead context, and subagent-launch failure after thread resolution.
- Verify the tests assert both returned outcome shape and persisted metadata behavior; no test should depend on real Agent Mail, real subagents, or wall-clock timers.

Edge cases & failure modes:
- Missing current bead ID must fall back cleanly to a run-level thread.
- Malformed or empty thread/reviewer metadata must not be persisted as a successful launch.
- If Agent Mail thread creation/message send succeeds but reviewer/subagent launch fails, return `degraded` or `skipped` and do not mark the review as launched.
- Repeated calls for an already-launched state or the same triggering head must be idempotent and produce no duplicate send.
- Unavailable Agent Mail, thrown exceptions, or partial response payloads must be surfaced as clear reason text while allowing the implementation loop to continue.

What to implement:
- Add a launch boundary that records thread/reviewer metadata and sends the full-review instructions produced by the core prompt builder.
- Use a current-bead thread when available, otherwise a run-level thread with an explicit reason.
- Return a structured result that distinguishes launched, skipped, and degraded outcomes.
- Preserve at-most-once semantics from the core state and never claim a review launched if Agent Mail or subagent launch failed.
- Keep Agent Mail unavailable/failing cases non-fatal: implementation must continue with a clear warning/result reason.

Key decisions and trade-offs:
- Agent Mail is the coordination source of truth because implementation agents can subscribe to bead/run threads without reading local temp files.
- Fail-open is required: review should reduce risk, not block all implementation when Agent Mail is unavailable.
- Metadata is recorded in state so downstream append/integration code can avoid duplicate launch or duplicate bead notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] At threshold, review launch attempts to coordinate through Agent Mail using a current-bead or run-level thread.
- [ ] The launched result includes thread ID, reviewer/agent name when known, launched head, launched timestamp, and reason text.
- [ ] The code uses a narrow injected Agent Mail/subagent boundary so unit tests can fully fake success and failure scenarios.
- [ ] Agent Mail failures do not throw through the implementation loop; they return a skipped/degraded result with a clear warning.
- [ ] Tests cover successful launch, current-bead-thread selection, run-level fallback, unavailable Agent Mail, malformed/missing current bead context, and subagent-launch failure after thread resolution.
- [ ] No final user-facing text claims review launched if the Agent Mail/subagent launch failed.
- [ ] The implementation does not create or update beads; append behavior stays in `fresh-eyes-current-bead-append`.

### Verification:
- Commands/checks:
  - `npm test -- src/agent-mail.test.ts src/fresh-eyes-review.test.ts`
  - `npm run build`
- Success looks like: the focused tests prove thread selection, structured launched/skipped/degraded outcomes, metadata persistence only on success, and graceful degradation without duplicate sends; TypeScript finishes with no errors.
- Manual proof fallback: if commands cannot run, capture the exact blocker and inspect the launch boundary plus tests to confirm the injected Agent Mail interface, explicit reason codes, no-false-success behavior, and idempotent state update rules.

title: Dashboard refresh controller
description:
## Dashboard refresh controller

### Context
The dashboard needs a controller that polls orchestrator data while work is active and pushes fresh `DashboardSnapshot` values to the UI layer. This bead builds that controller independently of the rendering layer.

This should be a scheduling/state-management bead only: no TUI rendering logic beyond calling `onUpdate(snapshot)`.

### Architecture guidance
Use a **single self-rescheduling timer** (`setTimeout`) rather than a fixed `setInterval`.

Reason: refresh cadence changes based on orchestrator phase, error backoff, and invalidation requests. A reschedulable timeout keeps those rules simple and avoids overlapping work or stale intervals that continue running at the wrong cadence.

### What to build

#### `src/dashboard/controller.ts` (new)
```ts
interface DashboardControllerOptions {
  readBeadsFn: () => Promise<Bead[]>;
  getUnblockedBeadsFn: () => Promise<string[]>;
  getState: () => OrchestratorState;
  getTenderSummary: () => string | undefined;
  onUpdate: (snapshot: DashboardSnapshot) => void;
  activeIntervalMs?: number; // default 3000
}
```

Export `DashboardController`.

Import:
- `Bead` and `OrchestratorState` from `../types.js`
- `buildDashboardSnapshot` from `./model.js`
- `DashboardSnapshot` from `./types.js`

### Required public methods
- `start(): void`
  - idempotent
  - begins the scheduling loop only if the current phase is not `idle` or `complete`
- `stop(): void`
  - idempotent
  - clears any outstanding timer
- `refreshNow(): Promise<void>`
  - performs an immediate refresh using the flow below
- `invalidate(): void`
  - coalesces multiple invalidations and schedules an immediate refresh on the next tick
- `dispose(): void`
  - stops timers and prevents future scheduled work

### Internal refresh flow
1. Read `state = getState()`
2. Call `readBeadsFn()` and `getUnblockedBeadsFn()` in parallel via `Promise.all`
3. Convert unblocked bead ids into `new Set<string>(...)`
4. Read `tenderSummary = getTenderSummary()`
5. Build a snapshot with `buildDashboardSnapshot(state, beads, unblockedSet, tenderSummary)`
6. Call `onUpdate(snapshot)`
7. Reschedule the next timer based on the latest phase / failure state

### Scheduling rules
- Active execution phases `implementing`, `reviewing`, and `iterating` refresh every `activeIntervalMs` (default 3000)
- Other non-terminal non-idle phases refresh every `activeIntervalMs * 2`
- `idle` and `complete` phases do not keep a timer running
- After 3 consecutive refresh failures, temporarily back off to 30000ms
- On the next successful refresh, reset the failure counter and restore normal cadence

### Failure / concurrency rules
- Never allow overlapping async refreshes
- If a refresh is already in flight and another refresh is requested, set a `pendingRefresh` flag so exactly one follow-up refresh runs afterward
- If `readBeadsFn()` or `getUnblockedBeadsFn()` throws:
  - do not throw from the controller
  - build a degraded snapshot by calling `buildDashboardSnapshot(state, [], new Set(), tenderSummary)`
  - ensure the delivered snapshot has `staleData=true` (the model layer should already do this for the active-beads-empty case; if needed, append an alert before `onUpdate`)
  - keep the controller alive and continue scheduling future refreshes
- Errors from one cycle must not permanently wedge the controller

### Tests to add
Create `src/dashboard/__tests__/controller.test.ts` using fake timers and mocks. Cover at minimum:
1. `start()` is idempotent and does not create duplicate timers
2. `stop()` clears timers and is safe to call repeatedly
3. `refreshNow()` triggers one immediate `onUpdate` call with a snapshot
4. parallel reads use both `readBeadsFn` and `getUnblockedBeadsFn`
5. in-flight guard prevents overlap and coalesces to one pending refresh
6. `invalidate()` schedules a near-immediate refresh but collapses repeated calls
7. idle/complete phases stop scheduling
8. implementing/reviewing/iterating use the fast cadence
9. non-active non-terminal phases use the slower cadence
10. three consecutive failures trigger 30s backoff
11. success after failure resets the counter and normal cadence
12. `dispose()` prevents later scheduled refreshes from firing

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/dashboard/controller.ts` exports `DashboardController` and its options interface
- [ ] Controller uses a self-rescheduling timer strategy that supports dynamic cadence/backoff cleanly
- [ ] `start()`, `stop()`, `refreshNow()`, `invalidate()`, and `dispose()` all behave as specified and are idempotent where noted
- [ ] Refreshes call `readBeadsFn()` and `getUnblockedBeadsFn()` in parallel
- [ ] Refreshes never overlap; pending refreshes are coalesced
- [ ] Idle/complete phases do not leave polling timers running
- [ ] Failure handling emits a degraded stale snapshot and keeps the controller alive
- [ ] Three consecutive failures trigger 30s backoff, and a later success restores normal cadence
- [ ] `src/dashboard/__tests__/controller.test.ts` covers the listed scheduling and failure scenarios with fake timers
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass

- `src/dashboard/__tests__/controller.test.ts` (new)

title: Dashboard render helpers
description:
## Dashboard render helpers

### Context
This bead builds the pure rendering layer that converts a `DashboardSnapshot` from `pi-i3b` into width-aware string lines for the TUI widget. Keep this bead side-effect free: no polling, no `ctx.ui`, no direct reads from orchestrator state.

### pi TUI Component API constraints
The pi TUI `Component` interface calls `render(width: number): string[]`. All rendering here must therefore be width-aware.

The `theme` object comes from pi's TUI theme system and should be treated as an object of string-formatting helpers such as:
- `theme.primary(text)`
- `theme.muted(text)`
- `theme.success(text)`
- `theme.warning(text)`
- `theme.error(text)`

Type the theme parameter as `any` in this module because the extension API does not export a stable Theme type for downstream extensions.

### What to build

#### `src/dashboard/render.ts` (new)
Export these pure helpers:
- `renderDashboardLines(snapshot: DashboardSnapshot, theme: any, width: number): string[]`
- `renderPhaseHeader(snapshot: DashboardSnapshot, theme: any): string[]`
- `renderProgressBar(completed: number, total: number, barWidth: number, theme: any): string`
- `renderBeadTable(beads: BeadSnapshot[], width: number, theme: any): string[]`
- `renderGoalLine(goal: string, maxWidth: number, theme: any): string`
- `renderTenderSection(tenderSummary: string | undefined, theme: any): string[]`
- `renderStaleBanner(snapshot: DashboardSnapshot, theme: any): string | null`
- `renderAlerts(alerts: DashboardAlert[], theme: any): string[]`

### Rendering rules
- Never emit raw ANSI codes; all coloring must go through the provided `theme`
- Width clamp behavior:
  - if `width < 20`, return a minimal summary layout instead of the full multi-section dashboard
  - the minimal summary must still include phase and progress information in a single compact line or a couple of short lines
- Status badges in the bead table:
  - `open = ○` using muted styling
  - `in_progress = ◉` using primary styling
  - `closed = ●` using success styling
  - `deferred = ◇` using warning styling
- Progress bar uses `█` for completed and `░` for remaining
- `renderProgressBar(0, 0, ...)` must not divide by zero and should show an empty bar
- `renderGoalLine` must ellipsize long text to `maxWidth`
- `renderBeadTable` must truncate titles to fit the available width, but keep bead ids visible
- If `beads.length === 0`, do not render an empty table header block
- `renderStaleBanner` returns a warning/error line only when `snapshot.staleData === true`
- `renderTenderSection(undefined, ...)` returns `[]`
- `renderAlerts([])` returns `[]`

### Suggested section order in `renderDashboardLines`
1. stale banner (if any)
2. phase header
3. goal line (if non-empty)
4. progress line + progress bar
5. alerts
6. bead table
7. tender section

### Tests to add
Create `src/dashboard/__tests__/render.test.ts` with a mock theme object whose methods wrap or identity-return strings. Cover at minimum:
1. full-layout render with repo, goal, alerts, beads, and tender summary
2. minimal-layout render when `width < 20`
3. `renderProgressBar(0, 0, 0, theme)` and very small widths like 5
4. goal truncation with ellipsis
5. bead-table truncation for very long titles while preserving ids/status badges
6. empty bead list renders no empty headers
7. stale banner shown only when `staleData=true`
8. empty alerts and empty goal produce safe output
9. unicode goal/title strings render without throwing

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/dashboard/render.ts` exports `renderDashboardLines` plus all helper functions above
- [ ] All functions are pure and side-effect free
- [ ] `renderDashboardLines(snapshot, theme, width)` returns `string[]` suitable for the TUI `Component.render(width)` contract
- [ ] No raw ANSI escape sequences are hardcoded; theme helpers are used for coloring
- [ ] Widths below 20 render a compact fallback layout instead of crashing
- [ ] `renderProgressBar` safely handles `0/0` and tiny bar widths
- [ ] Long goals are ellipsized and long bead titles are truncated to fit width
- [ ] Empty bead lists, empty alerts, and missing tender summary render cleanly
- [ ] `src/dashboard/__tests__/render.test.ts` explicitly covers the listed cases with a mock theme
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass

title: Dashboard integration into orchestrator
description:
## Dashboard integration into orchestrator

### Context
This bead wires the dashboard modules into the real orchestrator runtime. It should preserve today's widget behavior as a safe fallback while upgrading the primary path to a proper TUI `Component` that re-renders with viewport width and theme.

This bead depends on:
- `pi-i3b` for snapshot/model types
- `pi-ato` for rendering helpers
- `pi-6am` for refresh scheduling

### Important existing-caller constraint
`OrchestratorContext` currently exposes `updateWidget(ctx)`, and `src/commands.ts` calls it from `/orchestrate-status`.

Do **not** leave that caller behind. After this bead:
- `/orchestrate-status` must still show current orchestration status
- `oc.updateWidget(ctx)` should remain a valid entry point, even if it now delegates to `dashboardController.refreshNow()` or to the fallback renderer

### pi `setWidget` API
The extension API has two overloads:
1. `setWidget(key, lines: string[] | undefined)`
2. `setWidget(key, factory: (tui, theme) => Component & { dispose?(): void })`

Use overload #2 for the main path so the widget gets the current width via `render(width)` and can use the live theme.

### What to change

#### `src/dashboard/index.ts` (new)
Create a barrel that re-exports the dashboard public surface:
- dashboard snapshot types
- `buildDashboardSnapshot`
- render helpers needed by runtime integration
- `DashboardController`

#### `src/index.ts` (modify)
1. Import dashboard exports from `./dashboard`
2. Add `dashboardController` alongside `state`, `worktreePool`, and `swarmTender`
3. Replace the current inline widget update flow with two layers:
   - `renderFallbackWidget(state: OrchestratorState, tenderSummary?: string): string[]`
   - `updateWidget(ctx: ExtensionContext): void`
4. `renderFallbackWidget(...)` must preserve the exact information currently shown by the simple widget path:
   - phase line
   - repo line with scan source badge when present
   - truncated goal line
   - progress line when active bead ids exist
   - tender summary when present
5. `updateWidget(ctx)` should:
   - if no controller exists yet, call `ctx.ui.setWidget('orchestrator', renderFallbackWidget(...))`
   - otherwise trigger a refresh path suitable for current state (usually `dashboardController.refreshNow()`; if async fire-and-forget is needed, handle errors internally)

#### Dashboard controller setup
Instantiate `DashboardController` with:
- `readBeadsFn: () => readBeads(pi, cwd)`
- `getUnblockedBeadsFn: async () => { const result = await pi.exec('br', ['ready', '--json'], { cwd }); return JSON.parse(result.stdout).issues.map((b: { id: string }) => b.id); }`
- `getState: () => state`
- `getTenderSummary: () => swarmTender?.getSummary()`
- `onUpdate: (snapshot) => { ... }`

#### `onUpdate(snapshot)` behavior
Inside `onUpdate`, call `ctx.ui.setWidget('orchestrator', factory)` where the factory returns a Component that:
- captures the latest snapshot in closure
- implements `render(width)` by calling `renderDashboardLines(snapshot, theme, width)`
- caches rendered lines per width if convenient, but must invalidate safely when width or theme changes
- implements `invalidate()` by clearing any cache

Wrap this in `try/catch`. If the component-factory path throws, fall back to:
- `ctx.ui.setWidget('orchestrator', renderFallbackWidget(state, swarmTender?.getSummary()))`

### Lifecycle wiring
- In `setPhase()`:
  - `idle` => clear status, clear widget, stop controller
  - `complete` => set done status, clear widget, stop controller
  - active/non-terminal phases => set status, ensure controller exists/running, and request a refresh
- In `session_start` restore flow:
  - recreate/start the controller when restored state is in a non-idle, non-complete phase
  - do not silently lose the dashboard after resume
- In `session_shutdown`:
  - `dashboardController?.dispose()` before clearing references
- Preserve all existing worktree and swarm tender cleanup behavior

### Tests to add
Create `src/dashboard/__tests__/integration.test.ts` with a mock theme and representative state. Cover at minimum:
1. state + beads + unblocked set -> snapshot -> rendered lines happy path
2. stale snapshot produces stale banner in rendered output
3. fallback widget renderer preserves the old simple fields (phase/repo/goal/progress/tender)

title: Dashboard types and snapshot model
description:
## Dashboard types and snapshot model

### Context
pi-orchestrator currently renders a simple 4-line string-array widget via `updateWidget()` in `src/index.ts`. This bead creates the foundation for the richer monitoring dashboard by defining stable dashboard-facing types and one pure snapshot builder that converts live orchestrator state plus bead data into a render-ready structure.

Keep this bead strictly data/model only: no TUI rendering, no polling, no `ctx.ui` calls.

### What to build

#### `src/dashboard/types.ts` (new)
Export:
- `BeadSnapshot`
  - `id: string`
  - `title: string`
  - `status: 'open' | 'in_progress' | 'closed' | 'deferred'`
  - `priority: number`
  - `unblocked: boolean`
  - `reviewPasses: number`
  - `lastReviewVerdict: boolean | undefined`
- `DashboardAlert`
  - `level: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error'`
  - `message: string`
- `DashboardSnapshot`
  - `phase: OrchestratorPhase`
  - `phaseEmoji: string`
  - `repoName: string`
  - `scanSource: string`
  - `goal: string`
  - `beads: BeadSnapshot[]`
  - `completedCount: number`
  - `totalCount: number`
  - `tenderSummary: string | undefined`
  - `lastRefreshMs: number`
  - `staleData: boolean`
  - `alerts: DashboardAlert[]`

#### `src/dashboard/model.ts` (new)
Export:
- `PHASE_EMOJI: Record<OrchestratorPhase, string>` copied locally from `src/index.ts` so the dashboard data layer does not depend on runtime widget code
- `buildDashboardSnapshot(state: OrchestratorState, beads: Bead[], unblockedBeadIds: Set<string>, tenderSummary?: string): DashboardSnapshot`

### Snapshot-building rules
- Use `state.phase` for `phase`
- Use `PHASE_EMOJI[state.phase]` for `phaseEmoji`
- `repoName` comes from `state.repoProfile?.name ?? 'Unknown repo'`
- `scanSource` comes from `state.scanResult?.source ?? 'unknown'`
- `goal` comes from `state.selectedGoal ?? ''`
- `totalCount` should reflect the dashboard's current bead universe:
  - prefer `state.activeBeadIds?.length` when present
  - otherwise fall back to `beads.length`
- `completedCount` should count `state.beadResults` entries whose `status === 'success'`
- `lastRefreshMs` should be `Date.now()` at snapshot creation time
- Preserve the incoming `beads` order; do not sort inside the model layer

### Bead mapping rules
For every incoming `Bead`:
- `unblocked = unblockedBeadIds.has(bead.id)`
- `reviewPasses = state.beadReviewPassCounts?.[bead.id] ?? 0`
- `lastReviewVerdict = state.beadReviews?.[bead.id]?.at(-1)?.passed`
- `priority = bead.priority`
- `title` passes through untouched, even if extremely long; truncation belongs in render.ts

### Degraded / stale behavior
- If `state.activeBeadIds` has entries but `beads.length === 0`, set `staleData = true` and append a warning alert explaining that bead data appears stale or unavailable
- Wrap the entire builder in `try/catch`
- On unexpected error, return a degraded but valid snapshot with:
  - same `phase` if it can be read safely, else `'idle'`
  - `staleData = true`
  - `beads = []`
  - numeric counts defaulted safely
  - one `error` alert that includes the error message
- The function must never throw on malformed or partial state

### Tests to add
Create `src/dashboard/__tests__/model.test.ts` covering at minimum:
1. idle state with no repo profile and no beads
2. active state with multiple beads and unblocked set membership
3. `reviewPasses` pulled from `state.beadReviewPassCounts`
4. `lastReviewVerdict` pulled from the last review entry only
5. `completedCount` based on successful `beadResults`
6. `totalCount` prefers `activeBeadIds.length` over `beads.length`
7. stale-data detection when `activeBeadIds` exists but bead list is empty
8. missing tender summary and missing scan result default safely
9. very long bead titles are preserved unmodified in the snapshot
10. every `OrchestratorPhase` maps to a non-empty emoji
11. malformed inputs do not throw and instead return a degraded stale snapshot with an error alert

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/dashboard/types.ts` exports `BeadSnapshot`, `DashboardSnapshot`, and `DashboardAlert`
- [ ] `src/dashboard/model.ts` exports `PHASE_EMOJI` and `buildDashboardSnapshot()`
- [ ] Snapshot fields are populated from `OrchestratorState` using the rules above
- [ ] `completedCount` uses successful `beadResults`
- [ ] `totalCount` prefers `activeBeadIds.length` and falls back to `beads.length`
- [ ] `reviewPasses` and `lastReviewVerdict` are derived correctly per bead
- [ ] stale-data detection works when active bead IDs exist but the bead list is empty
- [ ] The model layer never truncates titles and never sorts beads
- [ ] `buildDashboardSnapshot()` never throws on any input combination
- [ ] `src/dashboard/__tests__/model.test.ts` covers the listed scenarios with explicit assertions
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass

- `src/dashboard/model.ts` (new)
- `src/dashboard/__tests__/model.test.ts` (new)

title: Enforce minimum refinement rounds before bead approval convergence
description:
## Context
The bead approval convergence logic in `src/tools/approve.ts` uses `polishConverged` and `polishChanges` to detect when to allow 'done'. Currently it can converge after just 1-2 rounds if the LLM outputs few changes. The `/planning-workflow` skill mandates: stop only when a round finds nothing AND you have run at least 4 rounds — NOT when the model claims convergence early.

## Rationale
Models become anchored to their own output and claim convergence prematurely. The planning-workflow skill shows that 4-5 rounds consistently find 11-15 new gaps per round. Enforcing a minimum (configurable) number of rounds before allowing auto-convergence prevents the most common failure mode: shipping a bead plan that the model said was 'solid' after 2 rounds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A constant `MIN_REFINEMENT_ROUNDS` (default: 4) is defined near the top of `src/tools/approve.ts` or in `src/prompts.ts`
- [ ] The convergence check in `src/tools/approve.ts` does NOT allow auto-convergence before `polishRound >= MIN_REFINEMENT_ROUNDS - 1` (i.e., at least 4 rounds have run)
- [ ] If the model produces zero changes before round 4, the tool still runs another round rather than auto-converging
- [ ] The 'Force approve' escape hatch (user can manually approve at any time) is preserved — minimum rounds only affects auto-convergence, not explicit user approval
- [ ] The round counter shown in the UI includes the minimum in parentheses: e.g. 'Round 2 of 4 minimum'
- [ ] npm run build passes and npm test passes (no regression in approve.test.ts)

title: Implement plan simulation core logic
description:
Create src/plan-simulation.ts with deterministic validation of proposed bead execution paths.

## Rationale
Before beads are approved, we should simulate their execution to catch structural problems early — cycles, file conflicts, missing references, and orphaned beads. This is purely deterministic (no LLM calls) and runs fast.

## Implementation

### Core functions:
1. `detectCycles(beads: SimulatedBead[])` — Kahn's algorithm topological sort. Returns cycle groups if any exist.
2. `detectFileConflicts(beads: SimulatedBead[])` — Find beads in the same parallel group that touch the same files.
3. `detectMissingFiles(beads: SimulatedBead[], repoFiles: Set<string>)` — Check that files referenced by beads actually exist in the repo.
4. `detectOrphanBeads(beads: SimulatedBead[])` — Find beads with no deps and not depended on (when >1 bead exists).
5. `computeParallelGroups(beads: SimulatedBead[])` — From topological order, group beads by execution level.
6. `simulateExecutionPaths(beads: SimulatedBead[], repoFiles: Set<string>)` — Orchestrate all checks and return SimulationResult.
7. `formatSimulationReport(result: SimulationResult)` — Human-readable markdown report.

### Algorithm details:
- Cycle detection: Kahn's algorithm (BFS topological sort). If not all nodes are consumed, remaining nodes are in cycles. Use DFS to identify specific cycle groups.
- Parallel groups: Assign levels based on longest dependency chain. Beads at the same level can execute in parallel.
- File conflicts: Only flag conflicts between beads in the same parallel group (beads with dep ordering are fine).

### Files:
- src/plan-simulation.ts

### Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] detectCycles correctly identifies cyclic and acyclic graphs
- [ ] detectFileConflicts only flags conflicts between parallel beads, not sequential ones
- [ ] detectMissingFiles validates bead file references against repo file set
- [ ] detectOrphanBeads finds disconnected beads in multi-bead graphs
- [ ] computeParallelGroups correctly levels beads by dependency depth
- [ ] simulateExecutionPaths returns a complete SimulationResult
- [ ] formatSimulationReport produces clear markdown output
- [ ] All functions are exported for testing
- [ ] npm run build passes

title: Add execution path simulation types and core logic
description:
Create src/plan-simulation.ts with NEW simulation capabilities that extend (not duplicate) existing validation in beads.ts.

## Rationale
beads.ts already handles cycle detection (via br dep cycles), orphan detection, file overlap among ready beads, and bottleneck detection (via bv). This module adds what's MISSING:
1. Topological execution ordering — a valid execution sequence
2. Parallel group computation — which beads can run concurrently at each level
3. Missing file validation — checking bead-referenced files exist in the repo
4. Consolidated simulation report — a single dry-run report combining new checks with existing validation results

## Implementation

### New types (in this file, not types.ts — keep types close to usage):
- SimulatedBead: { id, title, deps: string[], files: string[] }
- FileConflict: { file: string, beadIds: string[] }
- MissingFileRef: { beadId: string, file: string }
- SimulationResult: { valid, executionOrder: string[], parallelGroups: string[][], fileConflicts: FileConflict[], missingFiles: MissingFileRef[], warnings: string[] }

### Core functions:
1. computeExecutionOrder(beads: SimulatedBead[]) — Kahn's algorithm topological sort. Returns ordered IDs or throws if cycles exist (caller should use existing cycle detection first).
2. computeParallelGroups(beads: SimulatedBead[]) — Assign levels by longest dep chain depth. Same-level beads can run in parallel.
3. detectFileConflicts(beads: SimulatedBead[], parallelGroups: string[][]) — Only flag conflicts between beads in the SAME parallel group (sequential beads sharing files is fine).
4. detectMissingFiles(beads: SimulatedBead[], repoFiles: Set<string>) — Check referenced files exist.
5. simulateExecutionPaths(beads: SimulatedBead[], repoFiles: Set<string>) — Orchestrate all checks, return SimulationResult.
6. formatSimulationReport(result: SimulationResult) — Markdown report.
7. beadsToSimulated(beads: Bead[], depMap: Map<string, string[]>) — Convert Bead[] to SimulatedBead[] using extractArtifacts.

### Key design decisions:
- This module does NOT re-implement cycle detection or orphan detection — it assumes those run separately via validateBeads
- computeExecutionOrder relies on an acyclic graph (caller ensures no cycles first)
- File conflict detection is parallel-group-aware (smarter than existing ready-bead overlap check which only looks at currently ready beads)

### Files:
- src/plan-simulation.ts

### Acceptance Criteria:
